School & learning

future perfect tense noun

also future perfect, future tense (grammar), in the future perfect

modern

Traupman 226

futūrum perfectum

the future perfect tense

lēgerō, I shall have read (Traupman 226). This is a modern category. The ancient grammarians count five tenses and do not make this one of them: Donatus puts lēgerō in the subjunctive, as its future (eōdem modō tempore futūrō cum lēgerō lēgeris lēgerit, Donatus, Ars minor, Dē verbō), and Priscian treats it likewise. We have not found who first said futūrum perfectum or futūrum exāctum. The plain future is futūrum, tempus futūrum (Traupman 226, 246).

Other words

  • futūrum exāctum — the future perfect tense

    also used · modern

    The other usual name in modern grammars, “the completed future”.

See also tense, perfect tense, will.
